key_insight: V-PaSS improves perovskite solar-cell prediction by modeling absorber alloys and device stacks with physics-aware representations instead of treating them as simple categories.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable extrapolation to new perovskite compositions, unfamiliar layer stacks, and unseen laboratories, which is crucial for accelerating device design and screening.
method: Interpolates mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers from 23 relaxed pure ABX3 crystal-graph endpoints using Vegard’s law plus learned bandgap bowing.
Encodes device architecture with layer sequence, polarity, interfacial band offsets, and scientific-language-model embeddings for chemistry text.
Evaluates under an institution-grouped split to test generalization to completely unseen labs and materials.
evidence_signal: Under the unseen-laboratory evaluation, V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE, outperforming strong baselines and showing the largest gains on unseen alloys and transport layers.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable endpoint crystal structures and learned bowing parameters, so performance may degrade when those physical inputs are sparse or poorly characterized.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
